Aloha, my name is Irie! Growing up on the island of Oʻahu inspired my deep appreciation for the ocean, sparking my interest in marine science and conservation. In 2023, I earned a Bachelor of Science in Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Sciences and a minor in education from Oregon State University. During my time in Oregon, I primarily worked in the Tomas-Nash Laboratory investigating seagrass wasting disease and examining the reproductive effort of eelgrass beds at South Slough National Estuarine Research Reserve. I am currently in the Master of Marine Science program thesis track at Hawaiʻi Pacific University. My thesis evaluates the salinity tolerance and freshwater acclimation capacity of juvenile ʻUlua aukea, also known as giant trevally (Caranx ignobilis), aiming to inform the sustainable aquaculture and management of this species.
